subject: Request: Quarterly invoicing + extended payment terms for Peregrine (exec review)
messages:
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@peregrine.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>; priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: Laura Jensen <laura.jensen@peregrine.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Billing cadence and payment window for pilot

Hi Naomi / Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Peregrine is excited to move into a three-month pilot. Before we sign the SOW, we need to align on invoicing cadence and payment terms to meet our internal procurement. Two requests from our finance team:

- Quarterly invoicing (one invoice per quarter for the pilot)
- Net-90 payment window from invoice date (their standard for pilots)

I know those are outside standard Redwood terms. Happy to discuss tradeoffs — we can do a signed SOW and a PO up front. Please advise if Redwood can approve this for a pilot.

Best,
Ethan
Peregrine AI
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Billing cadence and payment window for pilot

Naomi — forwarding Peregrine's request. Summary and my recommendation below based on finance constraints:

Summary of external ask:
- Quarterly invoicing
- Net-90 payment window

Why this is risky:
- Longer DSO exposure for a new account (pilot, limited entity history)
- Quarterly invoices reduce cash flow visibility and delay realization of revenue

Recommendation:
- Offer a middle path: bi-monthly invoices (two invoices per quarter) + Net-60 for the pilot, with an option to revert to standard monthly Net-30 on production rollout.
- Require a 25% upfront payment or a signed PO committing to the pilot value as a risk mitigation (can be applied to first invoice).
- If Sales thinks Net-90 is necessary to close, request exec approval for a limited Net-90 pilot with a conditional credit hold and increased oversight.

If you want me to draft the exec ask, I can — include proposed language for discount/credit hold if needed.

— Priyom
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>; Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Billing cadence and payment window for pilot

Thanks Priyom. I agree with your compromise path. A few notes for the exec ask:

- We can make an exception for Net-90 only if we get either (a) an on-file irrevocable PO for the pilot amount, or (b) 40% prepayment.
- Approving Net-90 with no prepay would require an unusual credit concession and a revenue recognition note; I want the Sales leader and Finance lead to sign off.
- No discount should be tied to term extension unless Deal Desk approves a commercial concession. If Sales wants a discount in exchange for Net-90, they need to specify the percent and attach expected margin impact.

Priyom — please prepare a tight one-paragraph exec ask that includes: proposed terms, why this deviates from policy, mitigations (prepay/PO/credit hold), and a recommended approval (yes/no + conditions). Include the SOW and payment schedule attachment.

Naomi
Finance — Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>; Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Exec ask draft for Net-90 pilot (Peregrine) — ready for review

Attached: Payment_Schedule_Proposal.xlsx; Peregrine_SOW_v3.pdf

Naomi / Jonas — draft executive approval language below. Short and specific so it can go to the CRO / CFO inbox:

--- BEGIN DRAFT ---
Request: Approve a one-quarter pilot exception for Peregrine AI to be billed on a quarterly cadence with Net-90 payment terms.

Rationale: Peregrine is a strategic AI buyer that would run a high-usage pilot across multiple teams. Sales believes quarterly invoicing simplifies their procurement and is a gating item for signed SOW and pilot start.

Deviation from policy: Redwood standard terms are Net-30 with monthly invoicing; Net-90 and quarterly invoicing are non-standard and increase DSO and credit exposure.

Mitigations requested:
1) Peregrine will provide an irrevocable PO for the full pilot amount prior to first invoice OR provide a 40% prepayment.
2) Redwood Finance will place the account on a conditional credit hold if invoices remain unpaid 30 days past Net-30; escalation to Jane (CFO) at Net-60.
3) No discount will be applied for the term extension unless Deal Desk approves a commercial concession not exceeding 10% and Finance signs off.

Recommendation: Approve the Net-90/quarterly invoicing exception for a single pilot term (90 days) provided the mitigations above are in place.

Approvers requested: CRO, CFO, Head of Deal Desk.
--- END DRAFT ---

Please review and flag anything to tighten. If you approve, I'll route this to Jonas to include CRO & CFO in the thread and attach the SOW and payment schedule.

— Priyom
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>; Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>; Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@peregrine.ai>
Cc: Laura Jensen <laura.jensen@peregrine.ai>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 10:47:00 -0700
Subject: Exec approval request: Peregrine pilot billing exception

Team / Leadership — please see the ask below; this is ready for approval. I have included the external SOW and proposed payment schedule for context.

Thread id: DEAL-7821 (Peregrine AI)
Requested exception: Quarterly invoicing + Net-90 for a 90-day pilot
Proposed mitigations: 40% prepayment OR irrevocable PO + conditional credit hold/30-day escalation to CFO
Commercial concession: None currently proposed; Sales reserves right to request up to 10% off in exchange for extended term, but will return to Deal Desk for any discount.

Recommended approval: Approve the one-off exception for the pilot term only, provided prepayment/PO and the conditional credit controls are in place.

Please reply with APPROVE / DENY / APPROVE-W-CONDITION and any comments.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
